root_cause.text: The `bpf_fd_array_map_clear()` function lacks a scheduler yield point in its loop, causing the CPU to remain in an uninterruptible state for extended periods when processing PROG_ARRAY maps with many entries, which prevents RCU grace period threads from running and triggers RCU stalls.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `cond_resched()` inside the loop in `bpf_fd_array_map_clear()` at kernel/bpf/arraymap.c:1000. The CVE description explicitly states that "For PROG_ARRAY maps with many entries this loop calls prog_array_map_poke_run() per entry which can be expensive, and without yielding this can cause RCU stalls under load." The stack trace shows the RCU GP kthread was unable to run while the worker thread remained stuck in the loop calling `prog_array_map_poke_run()` repeatedly without yielding control back to the scheduler.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add scheduling points in fd array cleanup loop to prevent kernel scheduling latency and soft lockup warnings during large array iterations.
intent_record.what: Added braces around the loop body in bpf_fd_array_map_clear() and inserted a cond_resched() call after each __fd_array_map_delete_elem() invocation within the loop.
intent_record.how: The cond_resched() call allows the kernel to reschedule other tasks during iteration over potentially large file descriptor arrays, preventing long non-preemptible sections that could cause scheduling latency or soft lockup warnings. The braces are syntactically required to accommodate the additional statement.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by adding scheduling points (yield points) in the fd array cleanup loop. This prevents the CPU from remaining in an uninterruptible state during extended iterations over PROG_ARRAY maps, allowing RCU grace period threads to run and preventing RCU stalls.

candidates.rationale: This loop iterates through all entries in the fd array map without any scheduling yield points. When processing PROG_ARRAY maps with many entries, the loop runs continuously without allowing the scheduler to run, keeping the CPU in an uninterruptible state and preventing RCU grace period threads from executing, which triggers RCU stalls.

This function call is executed in every iteration of the loop without any cond_resched() or similar scheduling yield point between iterations. The absence of a yield mechanism after each deletion operation causes the CPU to remain busy without allowing the scheduler to intervene, leading to kernel scheduling latency and RCU stalls.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `bpf_prog_array_map_clear()` (lines 228-234) contains the vulnerable construct. It iterates through all entries in the array map with a for loop: `for (i = 0; i < array->map.max_entries; i++)` and calls `prog_array_map_delete_elem(map, &i)` for each entry. This loop lacks any scheduler yield point (such as `cond_resched()`) that would allow the CPU to be interrupted and RCU grace period threads to run. When processing PROG_ARRAY maps with many entries, this causes the CPU to remain in an uninterruptible state for extended periods, preventing RCU grace period threads from running and triggering RCU stalls. The fix is not present in this commit - there is no `cond_resched()` or similar yield mechanism in the loop.
